newsitem.title: USA: Boeing finds some shortages, delays - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Boeing finds some shortages, delays - WSJ.

text.p: Boeing Co, in its push to reach record production levels, is finding shortages of thousands of aircraft parts and delays in deliveries of some planes, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Thursday's electronic edition, the Journal said many of the problems are the result of demand pressures on the company's 3,000 parts suppliers and shortages of such raw materials as titanium.
One unnamed Boeing executive said there are about 500 parts shortages on the 747, and managers are "mildly concerned" about meeting June 30 deliveries for two jumbo jets.
Company executives told the Journal that the late deliveries will not be so severe to lead to penalties as called for in contracts with airlines.
"There's no doubt we are intentionally driving the system right to the ragged edge" to retain market share, Boeing's commercial airline group president Ronald Woodard said.
Woodard said Boeing plans to produce 43 planes a month by next April, an increase from 18 planes a monthly a year ago.
